title: Directional bias of the composition layer: attribution gradient and traversals
description: #1421 (July 2026) holds that machine composition carries an attribution-attenuation gradient, from named attribution through "some researchers" to none, and names probabilistic flattening; #1423 and #1643 (September 2026) hold that its errors fall one way, the names of the strong kept and those of the weak dropped. #1422 holds that composed answers supply interpretation without an obelus. #1460 (August 2026) holds that failures have moved from absence to ranking and temporal state, and specifies preregistered repeated trials and a machine-facing state layer; #1421 specifies PER as a comparative programme. The page also holds unrelated claims on the left and right hands, Pauline evidence, the lacuna mark, handwritten artifacts, a 2014 sonnet machine and a Hunter Biden memorandum.

finding.quote: “attribution gap” – the difference between relevant URLs read and those actually cited.
Drawing on approximately 14,000 real-world LMArena conversation logs with search-enabled LLM systems
No citation: Gemini provides no clickable citation source in 92% of answers
Perplexity’s Sonar visits approximately 10 relevant pages per query but cites only three to four.
the average query answered by Gemini or Sonar leaves about 3 relevant websites uncited

witnesses.shows: Search-enabled LLMs read more relevant pages than they cite, at rates that differ widely by system on the same queries; the authors tie the difference to retrieval design. This is the earlier pass's candidate C-0001, now verified; it precedes every claim it bears on and is an anticipation.
witnesses.does_not_show: Loss of attribution for a named author's concepts; AI Overviews as a surface; any skew of the loss by source size or standing; any trend over time.

claims.statement: **4.2 The attribution-attenuation gradient.** Adoption arrives with a gradient. The same framework, across captures, appears with full named attribution; with deflected attribution ("some researchers argue"); and with none — the concept stated as common fact. The gradient is not random noise: attribution attenuates as material moves from direct quotation toward paraphrase and synthesis, and as it travels from document-adjacent surfaces (retrieval with citations) toward pure composition (fluent answers). The gradient matters because it is the observable mechanism by which the next phenomenon is produced.
